732384201.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

732384202.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

732384203.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

732384205.text: Ooh, that's right. Despite its rather shabby appearance, it might still be some valuable antique!

732384206.text: We might be able to sell it for a good price at Royinjan's, right?

732384210.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

732384211.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

732384212.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

732384213.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

732384208.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

732384209.text: Paimon's not all that interested in this studying stuff, but if we can make a little this and that off their budget, why not, right?

732384101.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

732384102.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

732384103.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

732384105.text: Ooh, that's right. Despite its rather shabby appearance, it might still be some valuable antique!

732384106.text: We might be able to sell it for a good price at Royinjan's, right?

732384113.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

732384114.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

732384115.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

732384116.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

732384108.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

732384109.text: Paimon's not all that interested in this studying stuff, but if we can make a little this and that off their budget, why not, right?

732384111.text: Ooh! Maybe the people at the Theater could make use of this. But wouldn't they already have a lot of these instruments there already?

732384112.text: But y'know, it's not as if Paimon really knows the difference between drum types or anything.

732380101.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}. How have your recent travels gone?

732380105.text: I've heard about your previous adventures. It seems that you've become very experienced.

732380106.text: As long as you keep going, I believe that it will only be a matter of time before you become a truly great adventurer.

732380107.text: Hmm, speaking of adventures, we found this on one of ours.

732380108.text: This was left by some irresponsible adventurer. We thought it'd be bad if the commission he took never got resolved, so we brought it back here.

732380109.text: Hmm... Indeed, this item is key to a particular commission. Thank you very much.

732380110.text: The commission linked to this drum is a very important one from the Akademiya and is also critical to the expansion of our operations.

732380111.text: Unfortunately, though we have previously given this commission to various talented adventurers, they have all invariably failed.

732380104.text: It would not hurt to take a little rest from time to time.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the person near the camp

732380402.text: You guys don't look like tribespeople of the desert, more like adventurers from a faraway land.

732380403.text: ...But no matter who you are, this is as far as you will get. Please go back.

732380405.text: Commission? What commission? As far as I know, the Akademiya of the rainforest has declared this area a restricted zone. Why would there be commissions?

732380406.text: We were commissioned to investigate something up in the sky that looks like bad news! The Sign of... what was it again?

732380409.text: ...Wait. How did you come to know its name?

732380410.text: Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild told us! ... Hang on a minute. Didn't you mention the correct name just now?

732380414.text: Since you know of "The Sign of Apaosha," you must have heard of us "Shama{RUBY#[D]Order of Skeptics}niyya," right?

732380415.text: The desert past this point is a restricted zone under our guard. As a Ranger of the Order of Skeptics, I cannot let you pass, no matter what reason you may have.

732380412.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... How did you know of this name?

732380413.text: We are adventurers who have an organization at our backs. Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild told us, of course!

732383702.text: Lady Sorush... Why did you... You didn't have to attend to such trivial matters personally, let alone in front of these outsiders...

732383703.text: We Pari appear before whoever we wish, and our volition is not for you mere mortals to question. How dare you overstep your bounds!

732383704.text: (This little thing is about Paimon's size, and the way she talks is kind of funny... Why's Pyrrho calling "Lady" in that reverent tone?)

732383705.text: Hmph, your sins will be judged, but the time for that has yet to come. The two of you over there, as envoys of the Akademiya, it is only polite to state your names first, no?

732383706.text: Yeah, we should have introduced ourselves first, but that high-and-mighty attitude of yours is...

732383707.text: My words and actions are not contrary to traditions and principles of the Pari. The same cannot be said for you nameless persons... Hmph.

732383708.text: #Ugh... Fine! We're not nameless. Paimon is Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers who came here on a commission.

732383710.text: Hey! We adventure together all the time!

732383712.text: I need only know your names. Your other trivialities do not concern me. However, as for that drum...

732383713.text: #That item has a profound connection with us Pari, and is not something that you mortals should possess. {NICKNAME}, I command you to present it to me immediately.

732383714.text: No way! At least sound nicer about it when you're asking someone for a favor!

732383715.text: Besides, this item is important to our commission. We're to hand it to the leader of this Order of yours.

732383716.text: If we give it to you and fail to complete the commission because of that, not only might we lose our reward, we might even have to pay Mora to the Adventurers' Guild! That's a huge loss!

732383717.text: Reward? Mora? To think that you would risk your lives in a place fraught with peril for such frivolous reasons... You know nothing of what transpires here.

732383718.text: One mistake would send your race tumbling into an eternal samsara, and yet you commit deeds that are beyond even our comprehension.

732383719.text: You humans are such... interesting beings.

732383720.text: No matter... I shall bring you to the "leader" you speak of. This item would remain worthy tribute even if you should only present it to me after that meeting.

732383721.text: That's more like it... Wait, that's still not right! We still have to deal with that huge hole in the sky! And if we don't...

732383722.text: ...Huge hole? You refer to the Sign of Apaosha, then? And you wish to quell this calamity with mere mortal coils?

732383723.text: Hah, how presumptuous! It is the duty of us Pari to eradicate the Sign of Apaosha — an endeavor that I, Sorush, shall give my all to accomplish!

732383724.text: To quell this calamity, I must follow in the footsteps of the divine bird Simurgh, and sacrifice everything that one might call "Sorush"...

732383725.text: To stand in my way is not a sin that one such as you may bear!

732383001.text: What do you mean, "Dev"? Aren't these just Abyss Mages and hilichurls?

732383002.text: To think you would so easily defeat the rampaging Dev. Your strength is most radiant indeed. Consider me impressed.

732383003.text: Though there is still quite the gap between you and us Pari, the sight of you fighting valiantly reminds me of those humans of legend who once fought alongside us.

732383004.text: I have decided, then. You shall have the honor of being my Yasnapati!

732383005.text: Yasnapati? Paimon doesn't know what that is, but coming from you, it can't be anything good, really.

732383006.text: Do you not have such things amongst humans? Strategists, scribes, and the like? Those who exist to praise the heroes whose stories they exist in?

732383007.text: Neither of those jobs are what you just described!

732383008.text: No matter how great the hero, their great deeds must be recorded and sung of by others. If not, the same fate that befell ancient heroes shall befall them also...

732383009.text: Though they may have loved violence and conflict, great deeds are still great deeds, and they deserved to be remembered.

732383010.text: *sigh* Alas, those who loved conflict would be consumed by it, and once they had slain each other, they were all lost.

732383011.text: And because there were no authors or poets to tell of their deeds, once all who had lived in such times were gone, their works forgotten to the last. I will not be like them.

732383012.text: My great work shall shine so gloriously that the world itself will suffer great loss to not know of it. Thus, I shall now give you permission to record those deeds...

732383013.text: Rejoice and give thanks, for is this not a grace that few receive from us Pari?

732383014.text: This all sounds very complicated, but basically, you just need someone to tell you how awesome you are, right?

732383016.text: That's right! There's nothing worth bragging about with you. You just look kinda cute, that's all.

732383017.text: Your refusal is futile. Orders given by a Pari are absolute!

732383018.text: And what do you mean, cute? I am valiant! Heroic!

732383026.text: Whatever the case, it has been decided. Fret not, you shall be free to do as you please once I have sacrificed myself to restore the pure skies.

732383027.text: Till then, you shall witness my valiant form!

732383028.text: Well, sure, even if Paimon can't see it...

732383020.text: Hey, what are you talking about! Paimon doesn't consent to this!

732383021.text: Well, you are quite bright, aren't you? As I would expect of someone I have my eye on.

732383023.text: The Skeptics? I may admire their spirit, but other than their leader, whom you mentioned previously, the rest are not fit for such work.

732383024.text: They speak all day of how conflict is the true nature of this world, but they have themselves lost all ability to engage in such.

732383025.text: None of them will be able to witness my sacrifice to its end.

732383101.text: The path here is now dotted with Gray Crystals. When I last left it, it was not yet so.

732383102.text: Gray Crystals? You mean the crystals we're seeing everywhere?

732383103.text: Paimon's had her eye on them for a while now. What are they?

732383104.text: Gray Crystals are remnants of the black fire's embers. Proof that this land has suffered great calamity.

732383107.text: Indeed. I am sure you have heard that a great catastrophe struck long ago, where dark fire rose from beneath the earth and scorched the land.

732383108.text: The dark fire opened a bottomless hollow in this land, and the demons of Dev that crawled through that gap nearly turned this into a lightless realm.

732383109.text: Though the gap was blocked by the great tree, the dark fire's filth spread like seeds, and the countless dark and painful memories, released by that corruption, began to lay down roots and sprout.

732383110.text: This persisted till the honored lord of Khvarena, the divine bird Simurgh, drank the primordial water left behind by our god, before transforming herself into Khvarena of all kinds and scattering across the land.

732383111.text: From that day on, the Khvarena has taken the divine bird's place in defending this land, and those painful memories that leaked out have been sealed by Khvarena.

732383112.text: What was left are these ubiquitous Gray Crystals. Though they seem no different from any other stone, they may contain objects that are yet to be purified.

732383113.text: The Gray Crystals in the area have increased of late. I suspect that this must have something to do with the Sign of Apaosha's dark power.

732383114.text: But if we use Khvarena's might, we can get rid of these crystals.

732383115.text: If my senses do not deceive me, a wandering Khvarena should be nearby. Let us look around.

subQuests.subQuestName: Use the power of Khvarena to destroy the Gray Crystals
Go to the training grounds of the Order of Skeptics
Talk to the leader of the Skeptics

732381701.text: Lady Sorush, Khvarena's Envoy, you have returned.

732381702.text: Though it has taken much work on my part, the analysis of documents regarding the Rite of Chinvat will soon be complete.

732381703.text: According to my research, we need only collect all the Great Songs of Khvarena next, and your great work may then be completed.

732381704.text: Wait a moment. You two are...

732381705.text: #Do not fret. They are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, my newly-chosen Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} companion. They are here to witness my great work.

732381706.text: Hey now, Paimon hasn't agreed to that yet!

732381707.text: A Yasnapati, you say... Though I will not question your most astute judgment, I fear that allowing ignorant outsiders into this land before the Rite of Chinvat is complete may have untoward effects.

732381708.text: Know that the people of the Akademiya surely do not desire the Rite's completion.

732381709.text: Speak no further. I have my reasons for doing this.

732381710.text: #Well, then. Take that drum from before out, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

732381711.text: You bring the drum out, as agreed.

732381714.text: Hahaha! Yes. This is an important catalyst for the ritual needed to forge a Lau{RUBY#[S]connection}pa between ourselves and the Pari.

732381715.text: I have searched for many years for this, and to think it now comes to me! Ah, this is indeed a good omen for my future plans.

732381716.text: It would be good if the fates will also be with me when I lead the Order of Skeptics to throw down the Akademiya and burn their House of Daena, or whatever they call it, to the ground.

732381717.text: Wow. What a way to casually paint yourself as the villain, huh?

732381718.text: Villain? Hah! The Akademiya are the true villains here, have no doubt of that!

732381719.text: Ah, I forgot my introductions. I am Nasejuna, the Vijnanapati of the Order of Skeptics, we who cultivate ourselves here. If you would use the terminology of the Akademiya, I would be the equivalent of a "sage."

732381720.text: But I doubt those pampered folk would care much for what we at the margins call ourselves.

732381721.text: You do not look much like those the Akademiya might send.

732381723.text: Fair enough, though in truth it would not matter even if you were to be from that dratted place.

732381726.text: Even if the entire Corps of Thirty were to be sent here, my plans could not be halted.

732381727.text: Well, whatever your plans are, we didn't come here to stop them, that's for sure.

732381728.text: Hah! So they would all say, those treacherous louts from the Akademiya. And when my guard is down, you would stab me in the back!

732381729.text: Just like those people in funny masks who try to skulk about and steal our academic tomes.

732381730.text: They even dared to attack our honored envoy of Khvarena, Lady Sorush!

732381731.text: Hmph. And they met defeat at my hands, each one of them!

732381725.text: And so you are of them, after all. But it matters not.

732382101.text: Uh... Is that deep pit the Tunigi Hollow you were talking about earlier?

732382102.text: There's super huge crystals all over the place, even bigger than the ones we saw before! They look scarier, too...

732382103.text: These were once huge trees used to seal and subdue the creatures of the dark depths. The power of defilement has corrupted them, warping them into such forms as you see now.

732382104.text: Since the monsters have been sealed, it sure doesn't look like anyone needs to sacrifice themselves again.

732382105.text: That is why we must use the power of Khvarena to re-open the way...

732382106.text: Hey! Wouldn't that just release the monsters again? They took so much effort to seal, too!

732382107.text: No, no... I mean that we must open the path to the Sign of Apaosha. The way to the rift in the earth was sealed long ago. It can never lead to the true darkness again.

732382108.text: But that is exactly why that sealed rift does indeed connect to the illusion of the abyss.

732382109.text: We need only use the Great Songs of Khvarena to stabilize the seal before initiating the Rite of Chinvat to pass through the darkness and reach the Sign.

732382111.text: They are the mightiest manifestations of the Khvarena scattered throughout the world. We can use the Great Songs to initiate the Rite of Chinvat.

732382112.text: After that, we can open up a path to the darkness, just as legend holds that the first Vijnanapati Nagarjuna and the Pari did.

732382116.text: That's all well and good, but what will we do once we reach the side that the Sign is on?

732382117.text: I do not know what happens after that. I have encountered legends that our first Vijnanapati Nagarjuna was lifted up to the heavens, where he used divine power to extinguish the sign, but that, I feel, is mere myth.

732382118.text: I believe that Khvarena's Envoys will have some way. Since they can purify the defiling impurities, they must also have some way to extinguish the Sign.

732382119.text: Hah, did Sorush not also say that she wishes to imitate the sacrifice of Simurgh? The world is built upon conflict and sacrifice, after all.

732382120.text: Well that's what Sorush says, sure, but that's... that's way too irresponsible of you!

732382121.text: Oh, don't fret. Before the necessity of any sacrifice can be ascertained, we must still bring the Great Songs of Khvarena together. At the moment, we have yet to take even the first step forward.

732382122.text: Uh-huh, says the guy who's just been talking this whole time.

732382123.text: Well... Basically, only the Pari who has been chosen as a Bloomguard can touch the Great Songs.

732382124.text: But our current Envoy, Lady Sorush, has yet to obtain that right.

732382125.text: Is that so? For all that bluster, you really aren't all that, huh, Sorush?

732382126.text: You dare speak to me like that, Pale Floater?

732382127.text: Well, Paimon isn't a Pale Floater!

732382128.text: Only by obtaining the Twin-Horned Chaplet may she become the Bloomguard, a being able to gather the power of Khvarena. As such, she must first be acknowledged by Lady Zurvan, the First Pari.

732382129.text: She is a mighty Pari who once fought alongside our ancestors. It is even said that she was the very Pari who fought alongside the ancient heroes to subdue the embers of the Abyss.

732382130.text: But that elder of ours is... utterly unreasonable. She refuses to acknowledge my dearest desire. I'm afraid there's nothing I can do about that.

732382131.text: Still, even without the Twin-Horned Chaplet, my sacrifice will suffice to accomplish this deed.

732382132.text: Of course, I do not intend to doubt your desire to sacrifice yourself this way, but if you are unable to perform the Rite and pass through the dark hollow, your wish will not be fulfilled nonetheless.

732382133.text: However, I do have a suggestion. Lady Sorush called you her Yasnapati, did she not?

732382134.text: Why don't you go with her to the Vourukasha Oasis? That is where Lady Zurvan may be found.

732382135.text: Perhaps Lady Zurvan may yet change her mind should she see that we humans view Lady Sorush as the predestined envoy.

732382114.text: This is a ritual performed by the Pari that will allow us to open a path through the darkness. It is said that the first Vijnanapati, Nagarjuna, and the Pari did just that.

732382115.text: But we must first obtain the Great Songs and gather the power of Khvarena in order to initiate the Rite.

732382301.text: Whoa? So this giant snake fella is also sealed here?

732382302.text: Yes, but it does not have a "sinful form." Perhaps it was merely unlucky to have been caught in the crossfire and sealed here.

732382303.text: Well, maybe it's a good thing it's been sealed here. If not, it might just pop outta the ground and swallow us all in one go!

732382308.text: Hmm, you two certainly look like you get on well.

732382309.text: Of course, we're the best of buddies!

732382310.text: But is it not also said that even constant companions would fail to notice if the other was spirited away by a sprite? These stories are quite common too, yes?

732382311.text: #What are you talking about? {NICKNAME} would never do that.

732382312.text: Hah, I merely jest. If you are bosom buddies, surely some idle jokes will not move you?

732382313.text: Hehe. We shall soon reach the Vourukasha Oasis. Come, let us hurry.

732382307.text: Um, Paimon's not sure how to feel about that.

732382401.text: Whoa. The crystal here looks like...

732382402.text: Could this be one of those Wenut that we've seen before? How did it get trapped here?

732382403.text: Hmm? So you call these children of an ancient dragon the Wenut?

732382404.text: Still, it does not have a "sinful form." Perhaps it was merely unlucky to have been caught in the crossfire and sealed here.

732382405.text: Well, maybe it's a good thing it's been sealed here. If not, it might just pop outta the ground and swallow us all in one go!

732382410.text: Hmm, you two certainly look like you get on well.

732382411.text: Of course, we're the best of buddies!

732382412.text: But is it not also said that even constant companions would fail to notice if the other was spirited away by a sprite? These stories are quite common too, yes?

732382413.text: #What are you talking about? {NICKNAME} would never do that.

732382414.text: Hah, I merely jest. If you are bosom buddies, surely some idle jokes will not move you?

732382415.text: Hehe. We shall soon reach the Vourukasha Oasis. Come, let us hurry.

732382409.text: Um, Paimon's not sure how to feel about that.

732382701.text: Paimon didn't think there'd be such a huge patch of green on the other end of the mountain.

732382702.text: We were just in the desert, too. How strange!

732382703.text: Impressive, is it not? It is our homeland, after all.

732382704.text: The homeland of the Pari? So there'll be lots of other beings like you here, right?

732382705.text: Ugh, you know what? Paimon's not all that keen on going...

732382706.text: Should you not be excited beyond words?

732382707.text: And the big tree stump over there looks like it's holding off the stuff oozing outta that big hole.

732382708.text: That is the Harvisptokhm, the sacred form of the god that has granted us Pari life. It is not just some "large stump."

732382709.text: That's a god? Well, we've seen other gods, but this is the first time we've seen one looking like that.

732382710.text: That is because our go{RUBY#[S]Harvisptokhm}d cannot... be considered alive.

732382711.text: Five hundred years ago, our great god gave all to quell the power of the disaster afflicting this place.

732382712.text: But she was stained with corruption, and could not be reborn in a purer plane. Thus, her divine consciousness continues to wander the mortal one.

732382713.text: Our great god left us with the sanctified Amrita, and the Lord of Verdure caused the Harvisptokhm to grow from that, thus anchoring our god to this realm.

732382714.text: The Vourukasha Oasis has been nourished by the Amrita, and even the Khvarena that defends this earth gains its unending power by the grace of the Amrita.

732382715.text: But this god of yours doesn't look too well... She's been trying to hold out against the stuff coming out of that hole this entire time.

732382716.text: Her power maintains the seal over the dark hollow. I fear that the Sign has emerged here due to being attracted to her power.

732382717.text: If it were not for the presence of the Harvisptokhm, the defilement surging forth from that hollow would have infected the entire world... But it is also due to performing this duty that the tree has deteriorated so much.

732382718.text: I do not believe that I could ever bear to be reduced to such a state.

732382719.text: That is why I must leave a legacy of heroism behind for all to remember before it does happen...

732382720.text: Well, never mind that first. Let's go look for this Zurvan person, shall we?

732382721.text: If we get that Chaplet and fix the sky real quick, that might make your god feel all better too!

732382901.text: Well, if it isn't Sorush. Such a rare guest.

732382902.text: It has been a while... Elder Zurvan.

732382903.text: Elder? Well, if you call me that, then you should follow Pari norms and cease consorting with those humans whose hearts are heavy with their ulterior motives.

732382904.text: I haven't gone against our norms. I have only made contact with humanity to find a way to extinguish the sky-fire, just as the divine bird did.

732382905.text: And is that why you have learned all that claptrap about sacrifice from the humans? We Pari care nothing for such foolishness.

732382906.text: Isn't it our duty as Pari to sacrifice ourselves in the battle against the defiling impurity?

732382907.text: Await the call of destiny, Sorush. Only humans rush in blindly.

732382908.text: This destiny you speak of is a nebulous thing. I cannot simply be expected to sit and wait for it!

732382909.text: And that is precisely the danger. The Chaplet you seek contains the highest authority over Khvarena. In giving it to you, I may as well be handing the power of Khvarena over to those untrustworthy humans.

732382910.text: Can't you just have more faith in me, Elder?

732382911.text: Uh, you two... Looks like we're being left out here, aren't we?

732382912.text: Also, it seems like Sorush loses that cocky attitude of hers in front of Zurvan, huh? Hehe.

732382914.text: And those Skeptics are all too happy to go along with her, huh?

732382917.text: Well then, little ones. You came with Sorush, yes? This is not a place that ordinary humans may visit lightly.

732382918.text: Let me see... Well, you certainly aren't from the Order of Skeptics. You seem to be outlanders, in fact.

732382919.text: Well, in matters of courtesy, I suppose you two shall introduce yourselves first. I don't ask humans for their names often, you know?

732384301.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

732384302.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

732384303.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

732384305.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

732384306.text: Paimon's not all that interested in this studying stuff, but if we can make a little this and that off their budget, why not, right?

732384310.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

732384311.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

732384312.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

732384313.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

732384308.text: Ooh! Maybe the people at the Theater could make use of this. But wouldn't they already have a lot of these instruments there already?

732384309.text: But y'know, it's not as if Paimon really knows the difference between drum types or anything.

732384401.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

732384402.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

732384403.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

732384404.text: If we brought this one back to the Akademiya...

732384405.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

732384407.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

732384408.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

732384409.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

732384410.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

732389701.text: Then I shall leave the matter of the Twin-Horned Chaplet to you. I have some leftover work to take care of.

732389702.text: I believe that all people, no matter who they are, will submit to you and the Envoy's awesome glory.

732389703.text: When we have each done what we must, let us meet at the campsite upon the Temir Mountains.
